result.notes:
DEFECT 1 -- "register_scorer makes plugin loading non-idempotent" -- CONFIRMED AND FIXED.

Reproduced before touching anything, by running the reviewer's own /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP6/sim_wp7.py (WP7 step 1's load_plugins and WP11 step 3's register(), both verbatim) against the unfixed source: the first load_plugins(['fakeplugin']) succeeded, the second died with `ValueError: scorer kind 'partura' is already registered (pass replace=True to override it)`, and load_plugins(['fakeplugin','fakeplugin']) in one call raised identically. The mechanism is exactly as described: importlib.import_module is cached so the module body does not re-run and the factory object is the same object, but load_plugins calls register() again regardless, and the guard did not look at the factory at all.

Fix, scoring.py line 536 (now 540), the reviewer's suggested shape:
  if kind in SCORER_FACTORIES and SCORER_FACTORIES[kind] is not factory and not replace:
The FITNESS_KINDS check above it is untouched and still unconditional, so a built-in name is still refused even with replace=True.

Verified both directions through the same loader shape, not only at the API:
- same module loaded twice, and named twice in one load_plugins call -> both now silent (re-ran sim_wp7.py post-fix);
- two DIFFERENT plugin modules both calling register_scorer('partura', ...) -> still raises (/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/fix_WP6/clash.py). The guard still does the job it exists for.

I took identity (`is not`) rather than `==`: the design's WP11 factory is a module-level function, for which `==` is identity anyway, and `is` cannot be perturbed by a factory object defining a strange `__eq__`. A plugin that builds a fresh closure or functools.partial on every register() call would still collide with itself; that is a plugin bug and now has a clear message pointing at it.

I did NOT take the alternative the reviewer also listed (WP7's load_plugins dedups names plus WP11's register() passing replace=True), for the reason given: it needs two later packages to both remember, and replace=True inside a plugin would silently mask a genuine clash between two plugins.

Regression tests, both in tests/test_scorer_registry.py:
- test_registering_the_same_factory_again_is_a_no_op: the same factory twice (and once more with replace=True) must not raise, SCORER_FACTORIES still maps to it, scorer_kinds() lists it once, make_scorer still builds it; then a different factory under that name still raises and does not displace the installed one.
- test_a_plugins_register_hook_survives_being_called_twice: a plugin-shaped register() closing over one factory, called three times in one process -- the loader's actual shape.

THREE SUB-CLAIMS IN THE DEFECT'S "three flows hit this as designed" THAT ARE WEAKER THAN WRITTEN (the defect itself stands; these only matter if the coordinator reuses the reviewer's wording):
(1) "ALPHACUBE_PLUGINS=partura.ac_plugin together with --plugin partura.ac_plugin" -- this reads WP8 step 11's prose ("collect plugin names from args plus ALPHACUBE_PLUGINS"). The design's own main() snippet under "`--plugin` and the CLI" is `list(args.plugin) or [x for x in os.environ...]`, an `or`, so under the snippet --plugin SUPPRESSES the env var and that exact pair never duplicates. The design is internally inconsistent here and WP8 should settle it. The duplicate is reachable either way, because --plugin is repeatable (WP8 step 10), so `--plugin X --plugin X` alone produces it -- that is the load_plugins(['p','p']) case I reproduced.
(2) "WP8's own tests/test_cli_daily_and_plugin.py lists at least two cli.main([... '--plugin' ...]) cases" -- by my reading of WP8's test list, exactly one listed case clearly passes --plugin (the mine case); the others are --fitness nonsense, research/calculate with --daily-fields only, and an explicit no-plugin case. The count is overstated, though any second --plugin test WP8's implementer adds would have hit it.
(3) "Partura's idea_search.py ... would crash if load_plugins is ever moved inside the loop" -- correctly stated as conditional; WP11 step 6 puts the single load_plugins at start-up, outside the arm loop.

NOT TOUCHED (checked, found correct, left alone): the built-in-name guard and its unconditional precedence over replace; make_scorer's three-branch order and the unchanged PanelScorer fall-through; scorer_kinds()'s ordering; __all__; the dates/warmup forwarding. The other ten WP6 tests still pass unmodified.
